title: Existence of good randomness for derandomization
statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a finite probability space and let $X$ and $Y$ be finite input sets. Let $p$ be a public-coin finite-message protocol over shared randomness $\Omega$ with private inputs in $X$ and $Y$ and output type $\alpha$, let $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$, and let $\varepsilon, c \in \bbr$ with $c > 1$. Suppose $p$ $\varepsilon$-computes $f$, so that for every input pair $(x,y)$ the probability over $\omega$ that the randomized execution $\mathrm{rrun}(p,x,y,\omega)$ differs from $f(x,y)$ is at most $\varepsilon$. Then, writing $t = t(X,Y,\varepsilon,c)$ for the derandomization sample count, there exists a family $\omega_0, \dots, \omega_{t-1} \in \Omega$ of shared-randomness values such that for every $(x,y)$,
\[
  \frac{\#\{\, i \mid \mathrm{rrun}(p,x,y,\omega_i) \ne f(x,y) \,\}}{t} \;\le\; c\,\varepsilon.
\]
hypotheses_covered: Ω is a finite probability space
X and Y are finite types
p is a public-coin finite-message protocol over Ω, X, Y, α
f : X → Y → α is the target function
p ε-computes f (error probability ≤ ε for every input pair)
